newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: New venture will boost UPP output.
newsitem.headline: New venture will boost UPP output.

text.p: United Pulp & Paper Co Ltd's (UPP) new joint venture with Austria's Mayr-Melnhof Group (MM) will almost triple UPP's production of coated box board, UPP executive director Ong Seow Yong said on Friday.
Speaking to reporters at the signing ceremony of the joint venture, Ong said UPP currently produced about 60,000 metric tonnes of coated box board a year.

UPP and MM signed an agreement on Friday to set up a 50:50 joint venture company, called United Mayr-Melnhof Packaging Industries Pte Ltd (UMM), to set up plants in Asia Pacific to make various types of high value-added paper and board products.
UMM's first project is a plant in Singapore to make coated box board from recycled paper.
A company called Pacific Packaging Board Industries Pte Ltd (PPB) will undertake the Singapore project, estimated to cost US$80 million.
Ong said PPB, which will be fully operational in the third quarter of 1998, will produce about 100,000 metric tonnes of coated box board annually from recycled paper.
Based on current prices for coated box board of about US$500 per metric tonne, revenue from PPB would be about US$50 million when its new machine is fully operational.

Ong said PPB's export markets are in Asia; China is expected to take about half the output. Ong also said UMM is also currently exploring other opportunities in Asia especially in China, Malaysia and Indonesia.
He said the group hopes to finalise more joint ventures within the next 12-18 months in these markets.
UPP was taken over by Indonesian business tycoons Prajogo Pangestu and Bambang Trihatmodjo earlier this year.
